accepted.sentence: With an adjustable model, orient the handle so force bears against the fixed jaw rather than tending to spread the movable one.
Starting a nut by hand for several turns before applying the tool helps prevent cross-threading.
Pulling the handle toward the body is generally safer than pushing, since a sudden slip is less likely to cause a fall.
When a crowfoot adapter reaches an obstructed fastener, positioning it at right angles to a calibrated handle usually preserves the stated torque.
Some fasteners are tightened to an initial torque, then rotated through a specified additional angle to achieve the required clamping force.
After using an adjustable click-type model, return its setting to the manufacturer's recommended storage value to limit long-term spring stress.
Torque-indicating models need periodic calibration, particularly after a drop or severe overload, to keep their readings dependable.
Lubrication changes the relationship between applied torque and clamping force, so thread lubricant should follow the fastener's specified procedure.
